resolution.summary: Researched current firsthand community reports and official sources (2026-10-12). GitHub openai/codex #50430 documents POST chatgpt.com/backend-api/transcribe, Node fetch 403 cf-mitigated challenge versus Electron/Chromium 200 under the same authentication/network; #49351 and OpenAI Community topic 1404658 contain October 9 real microphone-to-text success reports on Windows and Ubuntu using VS Code's built-in http.electronFetch setting. This is a plausible transport explanation for our earlier Node-based 403, not proof of OpenCut success or quota entitlement. Current official codex-rs source includes RealtimeSessionMode::Transcription with gpt-4o-mini-transcribe; distinguish that from extension batch dictation. Third-party B4PT0R/codex-backend-sdk documents OAuth multipart /backend-api/transcribe support without a developer key, but is not an official API contract and explicitly rejects timestamps/SRT/streaming. Official Sign in with ChatGPT preview limitations explicitly exclude audio/video inputs and transcription API from the supported third-party Responses flow (https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source/preview-limitations). No further authenticated audio requests, product changes, settings mutations, or claims of long-file reliability/monthly-credit accounting. Concrete follow-up direction: isolate transport with bounded synthetic audio using native Chromium/Electron networking, and separately verify timing and account limits before product integration.
